rationale: This is a one-term substitution (dvt → dvt+prstkc) on the archive's existing winner DebtFinancedPayoutShortfall, which is close to the cosmetic-variant boundary and, because repurchases are far more transitory and lumpy than dividends, is more likely to dilute the commitment-defence content than to isolate a new economic choice.

The leg is internally coherent (accrual gap plus dividends is a genuine "cash-uncovered claims" construct) and the subsumption test is a legitimate question, but it is additively only one term away from the archive winner and stacks a leg (ib−oancf) whose debt-issuance interaction already failed twice in the archive, so the expected incremental information is modest.

This is a pure horizon-smoothing rescaling of the archive's winner with no new economic content, and the second leg is written misleadingly — TS_SUM(DELTA(x,1),3) telescopes to the simple three-year debt change — so the proposal amounts to a persistence robustness check rather than a substantively different signal.

Swapping the funding-source leg from debt to clean-surplus net equity issuance while holding the payout-shortfall carrier fixed is a genuinely discriminating test between the overvaluation and leverage-pressure interpretations, though the reviewer should note that net equity issuance alone is a well-known standalone anomaly so any result must be attributed to the interaction rather than the second leg.

The sign convention on recch/invch (Compustat reports these as decreases, so NEG correctly makes builds positive) is handled correctly and narrowing the accrual concept to the two most manipulable components on the cash-flow basis is a substantive repair rather than a cosmetic variant, but coverage should be watched closely since these line items are sparsely populated and format-dependent.

The use-of-proceeds mechanism is novel relative to the archive, but the MIN construct is only clean in its upper tail — its lower tail is triggered by *either* cash burn or debt repayment, so the low-rank states are economically heterogeneous — and the prior is weak since debt-funded cash hoarding is elsewhere associated with positive, not negative, expected returns.
